findings.evidence: `--first-parent` yields one line per merged PR in both merge-commit and squash workflows; `--no-merges` lists every feature-branch commit.
findings.fix: This says the same thing as the NEVER item 'NEVER combine `--no-merges` with `--first-parent`...'. Keep it in one place: put the workflow reason into the NEVER item, then delete line 37 and record the merge as a move, not a drop

findings.evidence: Rewrite each subject for the person who upgrades: what changed for them, not the internal wording.
findings.fix: The model already writes user-facing changelog lines like this without being told. Keep the sentence but tie it to the command's own rule: when a subject has no user-visible effect, it goes under Internal (the NEVER item about thin subjects)

findings.evidence: Step 5 gives output rules (one line per PR, at most 100 characters, merge same (#123)) but no way to judge user impact
findings.fix: Add one check before writing each line, for example 'Before writing a line, ask: would someone upgrading see or need to act on this? If not, move it to Internal'. This gives step 5 a way of thinking and not only formatting rules

findings.evidence: the log command in step 2 runs as `git log --first-parent --format='%h%x09%s' <to>` (no `<from>..`)
findings.fix: In the first-release branch, keep `%x09%b` (`git log --first-parent --format='%h%x09%s%x09%b' <to>`). Without it, the rule at line 35 that reads the PR title from a generic `Merge pull request` body cannot run. Also give the first-release form of the BREAKING CHANGE grep (`git log --first-parent --grep='^BREAKING[ -]CHANGE' --format='%h' <to>`), because line 42 assumes `<from>..<to>`

findings.evidence: If the tag resolves to the same commit as `HEAD`, rerun from `HEAD^` and use the older tag as the start.
findings.fix: Follow this branch to its header: `$1` was not given, so line 67 prints `Unreleased` even though HEAD carries a version tag. Add: 'In this case `<to>` is the HEAD tag and the header names it'

`%b` spans several lines, so the output is not one record per line, and the 'first non-empty body line' rule (line 35) cannot tell where one commit ends and the next begins. End each record with a delimiter, for example `--format='%h%x09%s%x09%b%x00'`, and split on NUL
